newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia right-wing group snatches guerrilla's kin.
newsitem.headline: Colombia right-wing group snatches guerrilla's kin.

text.p: A right-wing paramilitary group claimed responsibility on Friday for kidnapping the relatives of a Colombian leftist guerrilla leader.

An armed gang snatched the father, brother and sister of the People's Liberation Army's (EPL) second-in-command Bernardo Lopez Bustos on Sept. 2 in a district of Medellin, about 150 miles northwest (240 km) of the capital Bogota.
The incident was the latest in a wave of paramilitary strikes against the families of the leadership of Colombia's three rebel groups.

In a call to the Caracol radio network in Medellin, the so-called Peasant Self-Defence Group of Cordoba and Uraba, made up of cattle ranchers and peasant farmers based in Colombia's northwest, said it had seized Guillermo Lopez, 72, his son and his daughter.
Since late July, the same group has claimed responsibility for kidnapping three relatives of leaders of Colombia's largest and oldest guerrilla force, the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia.

The EPL, Colombia's third guerrilla force, took up arms in the mid-1960s. Most members of the group demobilized after signing a peace deal in 1990 but a splinter group continues fighting and is strongest in the banana-growing region of Uraba, close to Colombia's border with Panama,
Lopez Bustos, alias Victor, was promoted to number two in the rebel army following the capture of its leader Francisco Caraballo in 1994.
According to a report published last month in the weekly magazine Semana, one person is kidnapped every six hours in Colombia.

Based on data from Colombian intelligence service sources, it said 43 percent of kidnappings were carried out by left-wing guerrilla groups, adding that kidnappers had earned more than $530 million last year.
